title: When the Parish Sings
premise: True-crime podcaster Emrys Whitlock arrives in the fog-bound parish of Hollowmere to investigate its coldest case: the 1994 disappearance of choir mistress Ada Voss, whose body was never found. When the town's revered founder, Cornelius Ashgrove, is exhumed for a heritage survey and his coffin proves empty, Emrys realizes Ada's vanishing and the founder's false burial are threads of one buried secret. As Emrys peels back thirty years of alibis, they discover their own late mother sang in Hollowmere's parish choir and helped stage the empty coffin to protect a child born of a scandalous affair. In the climax, the last living conspirator—the town's gentle vicar—confesses that Ada chose to disappear rather than destroy the community, and Emrys must decide whether broadcasting the truth will save or shatter the only place they've ever felt they belonged.
about_author: Coral Fairweather is the pen name of a former rural correspondent who spent a decade covering small-town courtrooms and church suppers before turning to fiction. They write mysteries from a converted chapel on the Cornish coast, where the fog supplies half their plots.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Emrys Whitlock's POV. Emrys introduces their podcast and their perfect record of closed cases, choosing Ada Voss's 1994 disappearance as episode fifty. Arriving in Hollowmere by rain-soaked bus, they feel watched from the first cobbled street. Emotional beat: confident outsider masking a hunger to belong somewhere.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The B&B landlady, Mrs. Trelawny, offers warm bread and cold warnings: some questions aren't asked twice in Hollowmere. Emrys records the town square, noting how every local redirects conversation toward the harvest festival. Beat: charm with teeth beneath it.

chapters.title: The Choir Loft
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys visits St. Brannoc's church and finds Ada Voss's name still carved into the choir loft rail, fresh flowers beneath it—thirty years of tending. Vicar Nathaniel Pryce welcomes them with unsettling warmth. Beat: reverence shading into vigilance.

chapters.title: Episode One: The Woman Who Vanished
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys publishes the pilot; downloads explode overnight. But two interviewees call within hours asking to retract statements. A note appears under their door: LEAVE THE SINGING TO THE DEAD. Beat: thrill curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Reviewing old police files, Emrys maps the night Ada vanished—choir practice ended at nine; six witnesses swear she walked home alone. Every alibi is airtight, too airtight, like rehearsed lines. Beat: the detective's itch.

chapters.title: The Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. A heritage survey forces the exhumation of founder Cornelius Ashgrove for DNA archiving. Emrys attends, camera rolling, expecting pageantry. Beat: anticipation, the sense of history about to be disturbed.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs—gravedigger, coroner, Emrys. The coffin lid lifts on nothing but weighted sandbags and a hymnal. Gasps ripple through the crowd; the vicar's face goes white as candle wax. Beat: collective shock, the case detonating open.

chapters.title: Sandbags and Hymnals
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The hymnal in the coffin is Ada Voss's own, her initials inked inside. Someone staged the burial—and left her book as a message meant for whoever finally dug. Beat: revelation; Emrys realizes the grave was a letter.

chapters.title: Six Voices, One Lie
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys re-interviews the surviving choir members from 1994. Their stories align perfectly—until retired organist Gwendra Moyle slips about a 'second rehearsal' no record mentions. Beat: hairline crack in the wall of silence.

chapters.title: Mrs. Trelawny's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Trelawny POV. The landlady recalls the night Ada vanished: she saw a lantern moving toward the sea caves and said nothing because the person carrying it once saved her son's life. Beat: guilt kept warm for decades.

chapters.title: The Founder's Folly
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Researching Cornelius Ashgrove, Emrys finds he built the parish on money of murky origin and died conveniently rich, worshipped like a saint. His portrait's eyes seem to follow them. Beat: myth versus man.

chapters.title: A Voice on the Tape
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Digitizing an old cassette of the 1993 choir concert, Emrys hears a seventh voice singing after Ada's solo ends—a voice that shouldn't exist on the recording. Beat: spine-prickling discovery.

chapters.title: Threats in Three-Part Harmony
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Anonymous notes arrive set to hymn verses, each one more specific about Emrys's habits. Someone knows their room, their schedule, their mother's name—which Emrys never published. Beat: hunted feeling; personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Mother's Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Digging into their own past, Emrys finds their mother listed in a 1992 Hollowmere choir roster—she lived here, before Emrys was born, and never said a word. Beat: identity shaken to the foundation.

chapters.title: Gwendra's Second Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Gwendra POV. The old organist confesses there were secret rehearsals in the sea caves, lit by lanterns, where Ada taught songs 'for someone who couldn't come to church.' She stops short of naming names. Beat: confession half-swallowed.

chapters.title: The Child Who Couldn't Come to Church
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys theorizes Ada had a child out of wedlock—scandal enough in 1994 to vanish for. Parish baptismal records for that year are missing, torn cleanly from the register. Beat: the shape of the secret emerges.

chapters.title: Vicar Pryce's Sermon
chapters.summary: Pryce POV. The vicar delivers a sermon on forgiveness aimed, everyone knows, at Emrys. Privately he burns a letter in the vestry grate and prays harder than he has in years. Beat: a good man guarding a bad silence.

chapters.title: The Sea Caves at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys explores the caves, finding a bricked alcove, candle stubs, and a child's shoe fossilized in salt. Above it, scratched into stone: a line of music. Beat: dread and wonder entwined.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Digging
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys catches a hooded figure searching the cave alcove at night; a chase across the tidal flats ends when the figure vanishes over the rocks. They drop a brass choir medallion. Beat: adrenaline; the enemy has a body now.

chapters.title: The Medallion's Owner
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The medallion belonged to Thomas Ashgrove, the founder's grandson, who drowned in 1995—a year after Ada vanished—or so the record says. Emrys pulls the drowning file. Beat: the dead refusing to stay dead.

chapters.title: Drowned Men Don't Sing
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The drowning report lacks a body photograph; the coffin for Thomas was closed. Emrys connects it: an empty coffin for the founder, a closed one for the grandson. This family buries stories, not people. Beat: pattern recognition, rising excitement.

chapters.title: Interview with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Following a lead to a coastal nursing home, Emrys finds a resident matching Thomas Ashgrove's age who hums the exact melody from the cave wall. He calls himself 'Mr. Salt' and says only: 'She saved me. Ask her why.' Beat: electrifying near-contact.

chapters.title: Why Ada Sang
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Reconstructing events: Ada discovered Cornelius had fathered Thomas on her own sister, then covered a death—perhaps murder—to protect the family name. Her rehearsals in the caves were for hiding the boy. Beat: the mystery's architecture revealed.

chapters.title: The Podcast That Went Too Far
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Episode downloads hit millions; true-crime tourists flood Hollowmere, trampling the churchyard. Locals turn hostile; Mrs. Trelawny asks Emrys to leave. Beat: guilt—truth-telling has costs Emrys never priced.

chapters.title: Fire in the Vestry
chapters.summary: Pryce POV. An arson attempt guts the vestry, destroying remaining parish records. Pryce saves one ledger from the flames and hides it, knowing what it proves and who wants it ash. Beat: escalation; the conspiracy turns violent.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Pryce, torn, shows Emrys the salvaged ledger: monthly payments from Cornelius to Ada marked only as 'the singing lesson'—hush money that continued after both their deaths, paid by someone still alive. Beat: the conspiracy has a living head.

chapters.title: Following the Money
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Tracing the payments through bank archives, Emrys lands on a trust administered by solicitor Harlan Quill, the town's quiet fixer, who suddenly cancels all appointments and packs a car. Beat: closing in; panic on the other side.

chapters.title: Quill Runs
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys confronts Quill at the cliff road; he swerves, crashes, and in the wreck's aftermath clutches a photo of Ada and whispers, 'She made us promise.' He survives but won't speak. Beat: pyrrhic victory; answers just out of reach.

chapters.title: What Ada Promised Them
chapters.summary: Trelawny POV. Moved by the crashed car and the frightened town, Trelawny finally tells Emrys everything she saw in 1994: Ada alive, boarding a boat at dawn, choosing exile over ruin, leaving her hymnal behind on purpose. Beat: grief and release; the witness unburdens.

chapters.title: Ada Chose the Sea
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys reassembles the truth: Ada faked nothing—she simply left, and the town let her, staging the founder's empty coffin years later as a penance no one could read until now. But one question remains: who killed to keep it quiet? Beat: the moral knot tightens.

chapters.title: The Death in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. One entry in Cornelius's papers references 'the sister's accident'—Ada's sister didn't just lose her reputation; she died falling from the belfry weeks before Ada fled. It wasn't an accident. Beat: cold horror; a murderer walks free.

chapters.title: Belfry Bones
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Acting on new evidence, police reopen the belfry and find remains sealed in the clock housing—Ada's sister, hidden where only the choir would ever sing above her. Beat: grim vindication; the case is no longer cold.

chapters.title: Everyone's Alibi Breaks
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. With the death ruled murder, thirty-year-old alibis collapse one by one. Suspicion falls on the elderly choir circle—but each suspect is too old, too frail, too grieving. Unless the killer was younger than anyone thought. Beat: vertigo of suspicion.

chapters.title: The Youngest Voice
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys realizes the seventh voice on the tape belongs to a teenager: Harlan Quill's daughter, Rowan Quill, now the parish's beloved music teacher—the one person who had access, motive, and thirty years of trust. Beat: devastating realization.

chapters.title: Rowan's Requiem
chapters.summary: Rowan POV. Rowan, preparing the festival requiem, knows Emrys has found the thread. She rehearses her confession like a hymn: her grandfather Cornelius killed Ada's sister; her father helped hide it; she has spent her life paying the interest. Beat: tragic symmetry—music as both crime and penance.

chapters.title: Festival Night
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. At the harvest festival, the whole parish sings while Emrys and the police wait. Rowan chooses the moment of the final hymn to walk to the belfry rope, forcing everyone to choose between song and truth. Beat: unbearable suspended tension.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Emrys and Rowan POV, alternating. On the belfry stairs Rowan confesses publicly—not to murder, but to the cover-up—and reveals her father's deathbed admission: Cornelius killed the sister; Ada fled to stop him destroying the child, Thomas. The bell tolls as handcuffs close on history itself. Beat: cathartic climax.

chapters.title: What Emrys Broadcasts
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys edits the final episode through the night, holding the raw confession. Broadcasting everything would expose Thomas, still alive, and gut the town. Publishing nothing betrays their own creed. Beat: the loyalty-versus-truth choice at knife's edge.

chapters.title: A Different Kind of Ending
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys airs the full truth of the murder but shields Thomas's identity, ending the podcast not with a gotcha but with the choir's own recording—Ada's voice singing over the credits. The town doesn't forgive, exactly, but it exhales. Beat: bittersweet resolution.

chapters.title: When the Parish Sings
chapters.summary: Emrys POV, epilogue. Months later, Emrys stays in Hollowmere, renting Mrs. Trelawny's attic room, attending a service where a rebuilt choir sings a new hymn dedicated to Ada and her sister. For the first time, Emrys sings too—off-key, visible, home. Beat: belonging earned, identity claimed.
